# bbolt

```go
import "github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/stores/bbolt"
```

Package bbolt is the bbolt state\-store backend for blkit: a durable, embedded store keeping each run's ProcessState in a single file on local disk. See specs/state\-stores/bbolt\-state\-store.spec.md.

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/bbolt/store.go#L42>)

```go
func New(cfg Config) *Store
```

New opens (creating if needed) the database file and returns the store. Following the blkit constructor convention it panics on an invalid config or an unopenable file.

```go
func (s *Store) Close() error
```

Close closes the database file.

<a name="Store.Config"></a>
### func (\*Store) [Config](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/bbolt/store.go#L366>)

```go
func (s *Store) Config() (map[string]string, error)
```

Config returns an error: a bbolt file is local to one process on one machine and cannot be shared.

<a name="Store.CurrentVersion"></a>
### func (\*Store) [CurrentVersion](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/bbolt/store.go#L269>)

```go
func (s *Store) CurrentVersion(runID string) (*bl.CurrentVersion, error)
```

CurrentVersion folds the run's value records into the latest committed value per (task, field). Key order is replay order, so a single in\-order walk suffices. Returns (nil, nil) for an unknown run.

<a name="Store.Flush"></a>
### func (\*Store) [Flush](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/bbolt/store.go#L254>)

```go
func (s *Store) Flush(runID string) error
```

Flush is a no\-op: every Update transaction is fsynced on commit.

<a name="Store.FullHistory"></a>
### func (\*Store) [FullHistory](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/bbolt/store.go#L306>)

```go
func (s *Store) FullHistory(runID string) (*bl.FullHistory, error)
```

FullHistory walks both buckets in key (= replay) order. Returns (nil, nil) for an unknown run.

<a name="Store.Save"></a>
### func (\*Store) [Save](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/bbolt/store.go#L120>)

```go
func (s *Store) Save(meta bl.RunMetadata) error
```

Save upserts the run's metadata.

<a name="Store.WriteBatch"></a>
### func (\*Store) [WriteBatch](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/bbolt/store.go#L140>)

```go
func (s *Store) WriteBatch(ops []bl.WriteOp) error
```

WriteBatch applies the ops in one bbolt Update transaction — atomic, and durable when it returns (bbolt fsyncs on commit), which is why Flush is a no\-op.
